mode: scenario-adaptation; no upstream implementation or harness copied

mbuf-release.adaptation: Use Ker pool; require restored availability instead of skip.

clock-monotonic.adaptation: Use Ker monotonic nanosecond clock; no ff TSC implementation.

empty-export.adaptation: Verify zero-length copy export and ownership, not NIC transmission.

null-context.adaptation: Ker allocation rejects null context; no upstream ff consumption rule.

packet-export.adaptation: Verify copied bytes and lifetime; no ethdev send claim.

multiseg-boundary.adaptation: Ker currently rejects multi-segment adoption, preserving caller ownership; positive support deferred.

queue-isolation.adaptation: Two owner-worker Linux skb FIFOs; no reload generations or SP/SC DPDK ring claim.

queue-full-ownership.adaptation: Full FIFO preserves caller reference and pool availability; no drain-ring statistics claim.

export-exhaustion-retry.adaptation: Exhaust the real Ker packet pool, assert failed copy-out preserves the caller's output slot and skb ownership, then release one mbuf and require a successful retry. No mocked copydata or NIC send claim.

offload-metadata-rejection.adaptation: Ker explicitly rejects checksum-partial and GSO metadata it cannot export, preserves the skb and output slot, then succeeds after metadata is cleared. No offload execution claim.

software-checksum-completion.adaptation: Ker-specific software completion extension motivated by this upstream checksum-offload case: copy a linear Internet-checksum CHECKSUM_PARTIAL skb and complete its seeded transport checksum using Linux checksum primitives before export. CRC32C is rejected when the imported skb layout exposes csum_not_inet; GSO and the existing ordinary CHECKSUM_PARTIAL export remain rejected, and the copy carries no DPDK TX offload flags. This does not claim F-Stack's NIC/hardware offload behavior.

headroom-export.adaptation: Export a payload with explicit headroom, verify mbuf data_off and bytes, then free the skb and validate copy lifetime. No ethdev transmission claim.

multiseg-copy.adaptation: Use a real three-segment DPDK chain with uneven and zero-length segments as input to Ker's explicit chain-to-linear-skb copy adapter; verify source links/refcounts remain caller-owned and the copy survives source-chain release. This does not implement upstream's segmented TX path or Linux nonlinear skb support.

multiseg-ethernet-ingress.adaptation: Adapt the multisegment packet geometry intent in the ingress direction: split destination/source/type fields across real DPDK segments, copy to a linear skb, classify with unchanged Linux eth_type_trans and deliver one host packet through Ker's existing protocol runtime. Also verify broadcast/otherhost classification, ownership and failure boundaries. This is not F-Stack TX, NIC traffic, Ethernet offload or nonlinear Linux skb support.

arp-chain-feedback.adaptation: Ker-specific integration extension of the upstream multisegment geometry scenario: split a valid Ethernet ARP reply across a real DPDK chain, linearize and classify it, then exercise the existing ARP decoder and scoped native neighbor feedback from an actual worker RX poll. Verify rejection boundaries, timer/reference preservation, source-chain release and pool recovery. The ARP feedback scenario is not an upstream F-Stack test and does not claim NIC traffic or general ARP learning.

ipv4-ingress-validation.adaptation: Ker-specific ingress/header-validation extension. At pinned F-Stack revision 646a641cfff77f4815e1e29829a09e1ed15a2999 both named cases exercise ff_dpdk_if_send, not IPv4 ingress. Ker uses real segmented DPDK input and its copy/classify path, then validates IPv4 header/options, length, padding and native ip_fast_csum. No ip_rcv, routing, fragment reassembly, transport/socket or NIC delivery claim.

udp-ingress-validation.adaptation: Ker-specific ingress extension motivated by the pinned UDP checksum TX case. The F-Stack source only sets UDP TX offload metadata and calls ff_dpdk_if_send; it does not test UDP ingress. Ker validates an unfragmented IPv4 UDP datagram using the original Linux pseudoheader checksum primitives. This does not claim socket delivery, routing, reassembly, ICMP, NIC or TX offload support.

udp-minimal-boundaries.adaptation: Additional Ker-specific UDP ingress regression for the minimum eight-byte header with zero and valid nonzero checksums, zero-valued ports, even payload length and Ethernet padding exclusion. The upstream case is still TX-only and does not cover these receive semantics.

tcp-ingress-validation.adaptation: Ker-specific ingress extension motivated by the pinned TCP checksum TX case. The upstream case enables TCP TX checksum offload and calls ff_dpdk_if_send; it is not a TCP receive test. Ker validates an unfragmented IPv4 TCP segment and its complete pseudoheader checksum, preserving options as opaque bytes. This does not claim TCP option interpretation, connection state, routing, reassembly, socket delivery, NIC or TX offload support.

transport-receive.adaptation: Ker-specific worker RX integration extension motivated by upstream UDP/TCP TX checksum-offload cases; neither upstream case tests ingress. A registered ETH_P_IP handler validates and synchronously exposes existing immutable UDP/TCP packet views, consumes its skb reference on every path, and fails closed when protocol fanout shares the skb descriptor reference. This is not socket delivery, routing, fragment reassembly, TCP state or NIC receive support.

udp-create.adaptation: Ker-specific software packet-construction and receive-roundtrip extension motivated by the upstream UDP TX checksum-offload case, which is not an explicit-address UDP constructor or ingress scenario. Ker builds a fixed Ethernet/IPv4/UDP packet with Linux software checksum primitives, copies it through the existing export and segmented ingress adapters, then validates it in the worker-scoped transport receiver. No routing, address policy, socket, automatic TX offload or NIC transmission is claimed.

udp-neighbor-create.adaptation: Ker-specific neighbor-backed packet-construction extension motivated by the pinned UDP TX checksum case. The upstream case does not perform neighbor selection or ARP resolution. Ker uses one configured local address/device and an existing permanent neighbor entry, releases the lookup reference before allocating the packet, then validates software checksum and worker RX copy/retry behavior. No unresolved queue, ARP resolution, FIB, route, socket or NIC transmission is claimed.

tx-copy-export-retry.adaptation: Ker-specific worker TX copy/retry extension motivated by the pinned UDP checksum TX case. A bounded owner-worker FIFO retains each original skb until a sink accepts its checksum-completed or ordinary private mbuf copy; failures retry the pending head and cancellation returns ownership. The sink is an application copy consumer, not an ethdev/NIC, and no hardware offload or F-Stack TX path is claimed.

tcp-create.adaptation: Ker-specific explicit-address TCP/IPv4 packet-construction and worker receive-roundtrip extension motivated by the pinned TCP TX checksum-offload case, which is not a constructor or receive test. Ker writes fixed Ethernet/IPv4/TCP headers and software checksums; an application sink accepts a copy, then a real segmented chain is classified and validated by the existing TCP packet-view receiver. No socket, TCP state machine, route, NIC or hardware offload is claimed.

tcp-options-create.adaptation: Ker-specific extension of the pinned TCP TX checksum case: constructs fixed IPv4 headers with copied opaque TCP options and validates the software checksum through the worker receive path. The upstream case does not test option construction or interpretation. Options are not parsed, and this adds no TCP state, routing, socket, NIC or hardware offload support.

tcp-neighbor-create.adaptation: Ker-specific extension of the pinned TCP TX checksum case: derives the source IPv4/MAC from one configured address/device and the destination MAC from an existing NUD_PERMANENT neighbor, releases the lookup reference before allocation, then validates software checksums through TX retry and segmented worker RX. The upstream case does not test neighbor selection or ARP resolution. No unresolved queue, FIB, routing, source fallback, TCP state, socket or NIC transmission is claimed.

fstack-chain-export.adaptation: Ker-specific positive linear-skb-to-DPDK-chain copy extension motivated by the pinned multisegment TX case. Ker copies an existing supported linear UDP/TCP packet into independently owned direct mbufs, then validates the chain through its copy/classify worker RX path after releasing the source skb. The upstream case exercises F-Stack TX; this does not claim F-Stack/NIC transmission, Linux nonlinear skb support, or offload.
